title: Strong or weak password?
instruction: An attacker first tries well-known passwords and their variations. What holds out?

items.why: It's one of the most common passwords in the world. The attacker tries it straight away.
Short, and swapping letters for symbols is a well-known trick. Programs try it by themselves.
One word with the usual swaps. Attackers have dictionaries for that.

items.text: giraffe eats dumplings on the Moon
items.why: Long and made of unexpected words. That can't be guessed.
A popular game and a year. The attacker tries both among the very first.

items.text: the blue train rides backwards to Brno
items.why: A long sentence that you'll remember but nobody will guess.

items.text: The same long password for a game and for e-mail
items.why: When it leaks from the game, the attacker tries it on your e-mail too.

items.text: A long password from a password manager + 2FA
items.why: A random password and an extra second step. Even with the password, the attacker can't log in.

debrief: An attacker first tries well-known passwords, words and their variations. What holds out is a long password made of several unexpected words, or a password from a password manager, different for every account and ideally with 2FA.
